translations.text: In the beginning God created heaven and earth.
The earth was not visible [?]. There was darkness over the deep, [?] and the Spirit of God was moving back and forth over the waters.
And God said, “Let there be light.” [?]
“Let there be an expanse in the midst of the water.” [?]
“Let the water below heaven be gathered into one gathering, and let the dry land appear.” [?]
“Let the earth bring forth shoots of grass and a fruit-bearing tree that produces fruit.”
“Let there be lights in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth.” [?]
God made the two great lights.
He placed them in the firmament of heaven.
The fourth day.
God said, “Let the waters bring forth creeping creatures with living souls, and birds flying above the earth across the firmament of heaven.” And it happened that way.

God created the great sea monsters and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth according to their kinds, and every flying bird according to its kind. God saw that they were good.
He blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply upon the earth.”
Evening came, and morning came: the fifth day.

God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock and creeping creatures, and the wild animals of the earth according to their kinds, and livestock according to their kinds.” And it happened that way.

God created the wild animals of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the creatures that crawl on the earth according to their kinds. God saw that they were good.

God said, “Let us create a human being according to our image and our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, the livestock, the wild animals of the whole earth, and every crawling creature that moves upon the earth.”
God created humankind; according to the image of God he created them. Male and female he created them.

God blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and take dominion over it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of heaven, all the livestock of the earth, and every crawling creature that moves upon the earth.”
God saw everything he had created, and behold, it was very good.
And on the seventh day God rested from all his works that he had created.
He breathed a breath of life into his face, and the man became a living being.
God planted a garden in Eden toward the east, and he placed there the man whom he had created.
Of what is good and what is evil.
A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides into four branches.
The name of one of them is Pishon. It winds around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
The gold of that land is good, and there are carbuncles and leek-green stones there.
And the name of the second river is Gihon. It winds around the whole land of the Ethiopians.
And the third river is the Tigris. It flows toward Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates, the great river.
The Lord God took the man whom he had formed and put him in the garden to cultivate it and guard it.
And God commanded Adam, saying, “You may freely eat from every tree in the garden.
But you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. On the day you eat from it, you will certainly die.”
And the Lord God said, “It is not good for the man to remain alone. Let us make him a helper suited to him.”

And the Lord God again formed from the earth all the wild animals of the field and all the birds of the sky. He brought them to Adam to see what he would name them, and whatever names Adam gave to each living creature became their names.
Adam gave names to all the livestock and all the wild animals of the field. But for Adam no helper resembling him was found.
God cast a deep sleep upon Adam, and he fell asleep. God took one of his ribs and filled its place with flesh.
The Lord God made the rib he had taken from Adam into a woman and brought her to Adam.
And Adam said, “This now is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh [?].”
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and join himself to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.
[?] eat from it.
“As for the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, ‘You must not eat from it or touch it, so that you do not die.’”
The snake said to the woman, “You certainly will not die.
For God knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will open and you will become like the gods [?].”

The woman saw that the tree was good to eat from, pleasing for the eyes to look at, and beautiful to examine. She took some of its fruit and ate. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and they ate.
The eyes of both of them opened, and they realized that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together and made themselves coverings for their waists.
[?] the presence of the Lord God among the trees of the garden.
And the Lord God called to Adam and said to him, “Adam, where are you?”
Adam said, “I heard your voice as you walked in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid myself.”
The Lord God said to him, “Who told you that you were naked, unless you ate from the tree? Have you eaten from the one tree I commanded you not to eat from?”
Adam said, “The woman you gave me—she gave me some from the tree, and I ate.”
The Lord God said to the woman, “Why did you do this?” The woman said to him, “The snake deceived me, and I ate.”

The Lord God said to the snake, “Because you did this, you are cursed more than all the livestock of the field and the wild animals of the earth. You will crawl on your chest and belly, and you will eat earth all the days of your life.
I will put hostility between you and the woman, between you and your offspring and [?] her offspring. He will guard his heel, and you in turn will guard your head.”
He said to the woman, “I will greatly multiply your pain and your groaning. In pain you will give birth to your children. You will turn toward your husband, and he will rule over you.”

He said to Adam, “Because you listened to your wife’s voice and ate from the tree from which alone I commanded you not to eat, yet you ate from it, the ground is cursed because of your deeds. In sorrow you will eat from it all the days of your life.
It will bring forth thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
You will eat your bread until you return to the ground from which you were taken, because you are earth, and you will return to the earth.”
Adam named his wife Life, for she is the mother of all the living.
The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and these were put on them.
The Lord God said, “Look, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, then, lest he stretch out his hand and take from the tree of life, eat, and live forever—”
The Lord God cast him out of the paradise of delight to work the ground from which he had been taken.
God drove Adam out and made him live opposite the paradise of delight. He stationed the cherubim and the flaming sword that turns about to guard the way to the tree of life.
Adam had sexual relations with Eve his wife. She conceived and gave birth to Cain, and she said, “I have brought forth a man through God.”
She gave birth again, to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of sheep, while Cain worked the ground.
After some days, Cain brought God a sacrifice from the fruits of the ground.
Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his sheep and some of their fat. God looked favorably on Abel and his gifts.
[?] he will kill me.
The Lord God said to him, “It will not happen that way. Whoever kills Cain will pay sevenfold.” The Lord God placed a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill him.
Cain went away from God’s presence and settled in the land of Nod, opposite Eden.
Cain had sexual relations with his wife. She conceived and gave birth to Enoch. He was building a city, and he named the city after his son Enoch.
Gaidad was born to Enoch. Gaidad fathered Maiel, Maiel fathered Methuselah, and Methuselah fathered Lamech.
Lamech took two wives. The name of one was Adah, and the name of the second was Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal. He was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.
His brother’s name was Jubal. He was the one who made the harp and the lyre.
Zillah also gave birth to Tubal. He was a smith who worked with a hammer in bronze and iron. Tubal’s sister was Naamah.
Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, listen to my voice. Wives of Lamech, listen to my words: I have killed a man for a wound inflicted on me, and a young man for an injury inflicted on me.”
For vengeance was taken for Cain seven times, but for Lamech seventy-seven times.
Adam had sexual relations with Eve his wife. She conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Seth, saying, “God has raised up another offspring for me in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.”
A son was born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. He hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God.
This is the book of the creation of humankind. On the day God created Adam, he formed him in the image of God.
He created them male and female, blessed them, and called his name Adam on the day he created them.
Adam lived for two hundred and thirty years and fathered a son according to his likeness and his image. He named him Seth.
Adam lived seven hundred years after he fathered Seth, and he fathered sons and daughters.
All the days that Adam lived amounted to nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
Seth lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered Enosh.
Seth lived 707 years after fathering Enosh, and he fathered sons and daughters.
Seth lived a total of 912 years, and he died.
Enosh lived 150 years and fathered Kenan.
Enosh lived 715 years after fathering Kenan, and he fathered sons and daughters.
Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and he died.
Kenan lived 170 years and fathered Mahalalel.
Kenan lived 740 years after fathering Mahalalel, and he fathered sons and daughters.
Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and he died.
Mahalalel lived 165 years and fathered Jared.
Mahalalel lived 730 years after fathering Jared, and he fathered sons and daughters.
Mahalalel lived a total of eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.
Jared lived 162 years and fathered Enoch.
After fathering Enoch, Jared lived for eight hundred years and fathered sons and daughters.
Jared lived a total of 962 years, and he died.
Enoch lived 165 years and fathered Methuselah.
Enoch pleased God. Enoch lived 200 years after fathering Methuselah, and he fathered sons and daughters.
Enoch lived a total of 365 years.
Enoch pleased God, and he could not be found, because God had taken him away.
Methuselah lived 165 years and fathered Lamech.
Methuselah lived eight hundred and two years after he fathered Lamech, and he fathered sons and daughters.
All the days that Methuselah lived amounted to nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.
Lamech lived 148 years and fathered a son.
He named him Noah, saying, “This one will give us rest from our work [?].”
The Lord God said, “My Spirit will not remain in these people forever, because they are flesh. Their days will be one hundred and twenty years.”
When the Lord God saw that human violence had increased on the earth, and that each person thought about evil from childhood throughout all their days,
God said, “The time of every human being has come before me.” And the Lord God said, “I regret that I made humankind.”
“I will wipe out all creation from the face of the earth, from humans to livestock, from creeping creatures to the birds of the sky, because I am angry that I made them.”
But Noah found favor in the sight of the Lord God.
This is the family history of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation, and Noah pleased God.
Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth became lawless before the Lord God, and it was filled with violence because of them.
The Lord God saw that the earth was corrupt, and everyone had corrupted their way on the earth.

The Lord God said to Noah, “The time for all humanity has come before me, because the earth has become filled with lawlessness because of them. Look, I will destroy the earth together with all flesh.”
So make yourself an ark from squared timbers that do not [?], having four corners. Make it like this: compartment by compartment for dwelling, two and three. Coat it with pitch inside and out.
Make it like this: three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
Make the ark taper inward, and finish it to a cubit at the top. Make the door in the side of the ark. At the base and in three [?], make it compartment by compartment.
“Look, I will bring a flood of water upon the earth to destroy all flesh under heaven that has the breath of life in it. Everything that lives on the earth will die.”
I will establish my covenant with you. You will enter the ark, you and your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
From every wild animal, every domestic animal, and all flesh, bring two of each into the ark, so that you may keep them alive with you. They are to be male and female.

From the flying birds according to their kinds, and from all the creatures that crawl on the earth according to their kinds, two of each will come in to you. Keep them alive with you, a male and a female.
Take for yourself some of all the foods that you will eat, so that they may be food for you and the others.”
Noah did everything that the Lord God had commanded.
The Lord God said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and your whole household, because I have seen that you are righteous before me in this generation.
Bring in with you seven pairs of all the clean domestic animals, male and female, and two of each of the domestic animals that are not clean, a male and a female.
“And from all the clean birds, seven of each, male and female; from the unclean birds, two of each, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the earth.”
For in seven more days I will bring water upon the earth for forty days and nights, and I will wipe out all the creation that I made on the earth.”
Noah did everything that the Lord had commanded him.
Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
Noah entered the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives with him, because of the floodwaters.
And from all the clean birds, from the birds that are not clean, from the domestic animals that are not clean, and from all the creatures that crawl on the earth,
they entered the ark two by two to Noah, a male and a female, just as God had commanded him.
After seven days, the floodwaters came upon the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on that day the springs of the deep burst open, and the floodgates of heaven opened.
The flood was upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that day Noah entered the ark with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah’s wife, and the three wives of his sons with him.

And all the wild animals according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, every creeping creature that moves on the earth according to their kinds, and every flying bird according to its kind.
They went into the ark to Noah, two by two, from all flesh that had the breath of life in it.
Those entering went in, male and female from every kind of creature, just as God had commanded Noah. The Lord God closed the ark behind him from outside.
The flood came upon the earth for forty days and forty nights. The water increased and lifted the ark, and it rose above the earth.
The water grew strong and increased greatly over the earth, and the ark floated on the water.
The water grew very, very strong over the earth and covered every high mountain under the sky.
The water rose fifteen cubits above them and covered all the mountains.
Every creature moving on the earth died: the birds, the livestock, the wild animals, every creeping creature moving on the earth, and the people.
And everyone who had the breath of life within them, and everyone on dry land, died.

He wiped out every living thing on the face of the earth, from people to livestock, creeping creatures, and the birds of the sky. They were wiped out from the earth. Only Noah remained, along with those with him in the ark.
The water remained high above the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Noah and all the wild animals, livestock, birds, and crawling creatures that were with him in the ark. God brought a wind upon the earth, and the water decreased.
The springs of the deep and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the rain from heaven stopped.
The water decreased as it receded from the earth. It continued to diminish and decrease after one hundred and fifty days.
The ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on Mount Ararat.
The water continued to decrease until the tenth month. In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, the mountain peaks appeared.
After forty days and forty nights, Noah opened the window of the ark.
He sent out the raven to see whether the water had decreased. Once it went out, it did not return to him until the water had dried up from the earth.
He sent out the dove after it to see whether the water had decreased over the face of the whole earth.

It found no resting place for its feet and returned to him in the ark, because the water was over the face of the whole earth. He stretched out his hand, caught it, and brought it into the ark with him.
He waited another seven days and sent the dove out of the ark.
The dove returned to him in the evening with an olive leaf in its mouth. Noah knew that the water had decreased over the earth.
He waited another seven days and sent out the dove, and it did not return to him again.

In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the water disappeared from the earth. Noah uncovered the front of the ark he had made and saw that the water had disappeared from the face of the whole earth.
In the second month, the earth dried out.
The Lord God spoke to Noah, saying:
“Come out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons’ wives with you,

along with the wild animals that are with you and every living creature, from livestock to the birds of the sky and every creeping creature that moves on the earth. Bring them out with you. Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.”
Then Noah came out of the ark, with his wife, his sons, and his sons’ wives with him,
and all the wild animals [?] according to their kinds.
Noah built an altar to the Lord God. He took some of all the clean livestock and all the clean birds and offered them on the altar.

The Lord God smelled a pleasing fragrance [?] for the human heart is firmly set on seeking evil from childhood, at all times. “I will therefore never again destroy every living creature as I have done.”
“[?] Sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and spring, day and night will not cease.”
And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and rule over it.

“Fear and dread of you will fall upon all the wild animals of the earth, the livestock of the field, all the birds of heaven, everything that moves on the earth, and all the fish of the sea. I have placed them under your control.”
Every living, moving creature will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I have given you all of them.
But you must not eat flesh [?] with lifeblood in it.
Indeed, I will demand an accounting for the blood of [?] lives from every wild animal. I will demand an accounting for the life from his brother’s hand.
Whoever sheds human blood will have his own blood shed, because I made human beings in the image of God.
But you, be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and rule over it.”
God spoke to Noah and his sons with him, saying,
“Look, I myself will establish my covenant with you and your descendants after you.
And every living creature with you, including the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals of the earth that are with you—all those that came out of the ark.
I will establish my covenant with you: from now on, no living creature will die from the waters of a flood, and there will never again be a flood of water to destroy the whole earth.”
The Lord God said to Noah, “This is the sign of my covenant, which I will give between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all generations forever.
I will place my bow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of an everlasting covenant between me and the earth.
When I cover the sky with clouds over the earth, my rainbow will appear in the cloud.
And I will remember my covenant between me and you and every living creature of every kind. From that time onward, the water will never become a flood that wipes out all living creatures.
My rainbow will be in the cloud, and I will look at it to remember my everlasting covenant between me and every living creature of every kind on the earth.”
The Lord God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between me and every living creature on the earth.”
The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These were Noah’s three sons, and from them people spread over the whole earth.
Noah was a farmer, and he began to plant a vineyard.
He drank some of the wine, became drunk, and lay naked in his house.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness. He went outside and told his two brothers.
Shem and Japheth took the garment and laid it on both their shoulders. They walked backward and covered their father's nakedness. [?]
[?] his younger son.
Saying, “[?] is Canaan. [?] He will be a slave to his brothers.”
And he said, “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Shem. [?] Canaan become his slave.”
For this reason it was named Scattering, because there the Lord God scattered the language of the whole earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
These are the descendants of Shem. Shem was one hundred years old when he fathered Arphaxad, in the second year after the flood.
After fathering Arphaxad, Shem lived for five hundred years, and he died.
Arphaxad lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered Cainan.

After fathering Cainan, Arphaxad lived four hundred and thirty years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died. Cainan lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered Shelah. After fathering Shelah, Cainan lived four hundred and thirty years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died.
Shelah lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered Eber.
After fathering Eber, Shelah lived three hundred and three years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died.
Eber lived one hundred and thirty-four years [?] Peleg.
After fathering Peleg, Eber lived two hundred and seventy years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died.
Peleg lived one hundred and thirty-four years and fathered Reu.
After fathering Reu, Peleg lived two hundred and nine years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died.
Reu lived one hundred and thirty-two years and fathered Serug.
After fathering Serug, Reu lived two hundred and seven years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died.
Serug lived for one hundred and thirty years and fathered Nahor.
After fathering Nahor, Serug lived two hundred years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died.
Nahor lived seventy-nine years and fathered Terah.
After fathering Terah, Nahor lived one hundred and twenty-nine years and fathered sons and daughters. Then he died.
Terah lived seventy years and fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
These are the descendants of Terah: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.
Haran died in the presence of his father Terah, in the land where he was born, in the country of the Chaldeans.
Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarah, and Nahor’s wife was named Milcah, the daughter of Haran, who was the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.
Sarah was barren; she had not borne a child.

Terah took his son Abram, his daughter-in-law Sarah, the wife of his son Abram, and Lot, the son of Haran, his grandson. He brought them out of the country of the Chaldeans to go to the land of the Canaanites. He reached Haran and settled there.
All the days of Terah in Haran were 205 years, and Terah died in Haran.
The Lord said to Abram, “Leave your land, your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land I will show you.
I will make you into a great nation, bless you, and make your name great, and you will be blessed.
I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you, and all the tribes of the earth will be blessed through you.”
Abram left as the Lord had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was 75 years old when he left Haran.

Abram took Sarah his wife and Lot his brother’s son, along with all the possessions they had acquired and every person they had acquired in the land of Haran. They set out to go to the land of Canaan.
Abram traveled through the length of the land as far as the place of Shechem, to the tall tree. At that time the Canaanites were living in the land.
The Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I will give this land to your descendants.” Abram built an altar there to the Lord, who had appeared to him.

He left that place and went up to the mountain east of Bethel. He pitched his tent there, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the Lord God and called on the name of the Lord God, who had appeared to him.
Abram set out and traveled in the desert.
A famine occurred in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to live there, because the famine had become severe in the land.
As Abram approached Egypt to enter it, he said to Sarah his wife, “I know that you are a beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife,’ and they will kill me but keep you alive.
So say, ‘I am his sister,’ so that things may go well for me because of you.”
When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that his wife was very beautiful.
Pharaoh’s officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
They treated Abram well because of her, and he acquired sheep, cattle, donkeys, male slaves, female slaves, mules, and camels.
[?] that were severe, and his household, because of Abram’s wife.
Pharaoh called Abram and said to him, “What is this you have done to me? You did not tell me that she was your wife.
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now, here is your wife before you. Take her and go.”
Pharaoh ordered some men to escort Abram away with his wife, everything he owned, and Lot with him.
Abram left Egypt and went up into the desert with his wife, everything he owned, and Lot with him.
Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.
He went back to the place he had come from, through the desert as far as Bethel, to the place where he had first pitched his tent, between Bethel and Ai,
to the site of the altar he had made there at first. There Abram called on the name of God.
Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had sheep, cattle, and many livestock of his own.
The land could not support them living together, because their possessions were numerous, and they could not live together.
A quarrel arose between Abram’s herdsmen and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land.
Abram said to Lot, “Do not let there be fighting between me and you, or between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, because we are relatives.”
Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.”
Lot looked up and saw the whole region around the Jordan, that it was all well watered, before God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. It was like paradise and like the land of Egypt as you approach Zoar.
Lot chose for himself the whole region around the Jordan. Lot set out from that place toward the east, and they separated from one another.
Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot settled in the city of the surrounding region and lived in Sodom.
The people of Sodom were wicked and very sinful before the Lord.
After Lot had separated from him, God said to Abram, “Look up from the place where you now are, toward the north, the west, the east, and the sea.
For I will give all the land that you see to you and your descendants forever.
I will make your descendants like the dust of the earth. If anyone can count the dust of the earth, then your descendants too can be counted.
Get up and explore the land through its length and its width, for I will give it to you and your descendants forever.”
Abram moved away and came and settled beneath the tree of Mamre, which was in Hebron. There he built an altar to the Lord.
This happened during the reign of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of the nations:
They waged war against Balak king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
All these joined together in the Salt Valley, which is the Salt Sea.
They served Chedorlaomer for twelve years, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer came with the kings who were with him. They defeated the giants who lived in Ashteroth-karnaim, together with strong nations among them, and the Emim who lived in the city of Shaveh,
and the Horites who lived in the mountain country of Seir, as far as the terebinth tree of Paran, which is in the wilderness.
They turned back and came to the spring of judgment, that is, Kadesh, and they devastated [?].
The king of Sodom came out to meet Abram after he returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, in the Valley of Shaveh, which is the King’s Plain.
Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
He blessed Abram, saying, “Blessed is Abram by God Most High, who created heaven and earth.
And blessed is God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hands.” And he gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, but take the horses for yourself.”
Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I will raise my hand to God Most High, who created heaven and earth,
and swear that I will not take anything that belongs to you, from a thread to a sandal strap, so that you cannot say, ‘I made Abram rich.’
The only exceptions are what the young men have eaten and the share of the men who came with me: Eshcol, Aner, and Mamre. They will take their share.”
After these things, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your protector. Your reward will be very great.”
Abram said, “Lord, what will you give me? I will die childless, and the son of Masek, my home-born maidservant, is this Eliezer of Damascus.”
Abram said, “Since you have not given me offspring, my home-born servant will inherit from me.”
Immediately the voice of God came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir. Rather, the one who comes from your own body will be your heir.”
He brought him outside and said to him, “Look up at the sky and count the stars. See whether you can count them.” He said to him, “That is how your descendants will be.”
Abram believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
He said to him, “I am God, who brought you out of the land of the Chaldeans to give you this land to inherit.”
He said, “Lord God, how will I know that I will inherit it?”
He said to him, “Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a pigeon.”
He brought him all these, cut them in half, and laid the halves opposite one another. But he did not cut the birds in half.
Birds came down from the sky onto the divided bodies, and Abram spread himself out over them.
As the sun was about to set, a trance came over Abram, and suddenly a great, dark terror fell upon him.
Abram was told, “Know for certain that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs. They will be enslaved, afflicted, and humiliated for four hundred years.
But I myself will judge the nation they serve as slaves. After this, they will come out to this place with many possessions.
But you will go to your ancestors in peace, having been cared for into a good old age.
In the fourth generation they will return here, for the sins of the Amorites have not yet reached their full measure.”
As the sun was setting, a flame appeared, and suddenly there was a smoking oven, and fiery torches passed between the divided bodies.
On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, “I will give this land to your descendants, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates:
the Kenites, the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites,
the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaim,
the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.”
Sarai, Abram’s wife, had not borne him a child. She had an Egyptian slave woman whose name was Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram in the land of Canaan, “Look, the Lord has prevented me from giving birth. Go in to my slave woman, then, so that you may have children through her.” Abram listened to Sarai.
Sarah, Abram’s wife, took Hagar, her Egyptian slave, after she had lived with Abram in the land of Canaan for ten years, and gave her to Abram, her husband, as a wife.
He went in to Hagar, and she became pregnant. When she saw that she was pregnant, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
Sarah said to Abram, “I am suffering injustice because of you. I gave my slave into your hands, and when she saw that she was pregnant, I was despised in her eyes. May God judge between me and you.”
Abram said to Sarah, “Look, your slave is in your hands. Do to her as you please.” Sarah mistreated her, and she fled from her presence.
The angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, on the land along the road to Shur.

God appeared to him by the tree of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent at noon.
He looked up and saw three men standing near him. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed with his face to the ground.
He said to them, “My lords, if I have found favor in your sight, do not pass your servant by.
Let some water be brought so that they can wash your feet, and rest under this tree.
I will bring some bread for you to eat, and afterward you can go on your way, since you have turned aside to your servant.” They said, “Do as you have said.”
Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah and said to her, “Hurry! Knead three measures of fine flour and make them into cakes baked in the ashes.”
Abraham ran to the cattle and took a tender, fine calf. He gave it to the servant, who hurried to prepare it.
He took butter and milk and the calf he had prepared and set them before them. They ate while he stood beside them under the tree.
He said to him, “Where is Sarah, your wife?” He answered, “There she is, in the tent.”
He said to him, “I will return to you at this time next year, and Sarah, your wife, will give birth to a son.” Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were old and advanced in years, and Sarah’s menstrual periods had stopped.
Sarah laughed to herself, saying, “This has never happened to me until now, and my husband has grown old.”
The Lord said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh to herself, saying, ‘Will I give birth when I have grown old?’
Is anything impossible for God? I will return to you at this time next year, and Sarah will have a son.”
Sarah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. But he said, “No, you did laugh.”
The men got up from that place and looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah. Abraham was walking with them to see them off.
The Lord said, “Shall I hide from Abraham, my servant, what I am going to do?
Abraham will certainly become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed through him.

For I knew that Abraham would instruct his children and his household after him to keep the ways of the Lord, doing what is right and just, so that the Lord would bring upon Abraham everything he had promised him.”
The Lord said, “The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah has reached me, and their sins are very great.
So I will go down and see whether their deeds fully match the outcry that is reaching me. If not, I will know.”
The men turned away from there and went to Sodom, but Abraham was still standing before the Lord.
Abraham came closer and said, “Do not destroy the righteous along with the ungodly, so that the righteous suffer the same fate as the ungodly.
If there are fifty righteous people in this city, will you destroy them and not spare the whole place for the sake of those fifty righteous people, if they are in it?
Do not do such a thing, killing the righteous along with the ungodly, so that the righteous suffer the same fate as the ungodly. No! You who judge the whole earth must not pass such a judgment.”
The Lord said, “If I find fifty righteous people in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
Abraham answered, “Now I have begun to speak with my Lord, although I am dust and ashes.
But if the fifty righteous people are five short, will you destroy the whole city because of those five?” He said, “I will not destroy them if I find forty-five there.”
He continued speaking with him and said, “What if forty are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy them for the sake of the forty.”
He said, “Lord, may I speak? What if thirty are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy them if I find thirty there.”
He said, “Since I have undertaken to speak with my Lord, what if twenty are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy them for the sake of the twenty.”
He said, “Lord, may I speak once more? What if ten are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy them for the sake of the ten.”
The Lord departed when he had finished speaking with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his own place.
The two angels came to Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them and bowed with his face to the ground.

He said, “Please, my lords, turn aside into your servant’s house, rest, and wash your feet. Then rise early and go on your way, since you have come to your servant.” They said, “No, we will stay in the streets.”
He urged them strongly, and they turned aside to him and entered his house. He prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread for them, and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, from young to old, all the people together.
They called Lot outside and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we can have sex with them.”
Lot went out to them at the doorway and shut the door behind him.
He said to them, “No, my brothers! Do not do evil.”
“I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. I will bring them out to you, and you may do to them whatever pleases you. Only do not harm these men, because they have come under my roof.”

They said to him, “Move aside!” They said to him, “You came here to live with us. Are you now passing judgment? Now we will treat you worse than them!” They pressed violently against Lot and came forward to break down the door.
But the men reached out their hands and pulled Lot inside the house with them, and they shut the door of the house.
They struck the men at the doorway of the house with blindness, from the smallest to the greatest, and they gave up searching for the door.
The men said to Lot, “Whoever you have here—a son-in-law, a son, a daughter, or anyone belonging to you in this city—bring them out of this place.”
“For we are going to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has risen before the Lord, and the Lord has sent us to destroy it.”

Lot went out and spoke with his sons-in-law, who had married his daughters. He said to them, “Get up and leave this place, because the Lord is going to destroy the city.” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.
As dawn was approaching, the angels urged Lot, saying, “Get up and take your wife and your two daughters who are with you, so that you too will not be destroyed because of the city's lawlessness.”
They became troubled, and the angels took hold of his hand, his wife’s hand, and the hands of his two daughters, because the Lord had mercy on them.

When they had brought them outside the city, they said to him, “Escape and save your life! Do not look back or stop anywhere in the surrounding region. Escape to the mountain, or you may be swept away with them.”
Lot said to them, “I beg you, Lord!

Since your servant has found favor in your sight, and you have greatly increased the righteousness you show me by saving my life, I cannot escape to the mountain, or disaster may overtake me and I may die.
Look, this city is near enough for me to go there, and it is small. I will escape there—isn't it small?—and my life will be preserved because of you.”
He said to him, “Look, I have shown you favor in this matter too: I will not destroy the city you have spoken about.”
“Hurry, then, and escape to that place, because I cannot do anything until you go there.” That is why that city was named Zoar.
The sun rose over the earth, and Lot entered Zoar.
The Lord rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah from heaven, from the Lord.
He destroyed the cities and all the surrounding area, along with everyone living in the cities and everything growing from the ground.
But his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
Abraham went early in the morning to the place where he had stood before the Lord.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and over all the land of the surrounding region. He saw smoke rising over the land like smoke from a furnace.
When God destroyed all the cities in the surrounding area, God remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the destruction, when the Lord overthrew the cities where Lot had lived.
Lot went up to Zoar and settled in the mountain, with his two daughters, because they were afraid to live in Zoar. He lived in a cave, with his two daughters.
The older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no one on earth who will come in to us as is customary throughout the earth.
Come, let us give our father wine to drink and sleep with him, so that we may produce offspring for ourselves through our father.”
They gave their father wine to drink that night. The older daughter went in and slept with her father that night, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day, the older daughter said to the younger, “Look, I slept with our father last night. Let us give him wine to drink again tonight, and you too go in and sleep with him, so that we may produce offspring through our father.”
They gave their father wine to drink on that other night too. The younger daughter went in and slept with her father that night, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
Lot’s two daughters became pregnant by their father.
Abraham left that place and went to the land of [?]. He settled between Kadesh and Shur and stayed near Gerar as a foreigner.
Abraham said about Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
God came to Abimelech at night in a dream and said to him, “Look, you will die because of the woman you have taken, for she lives with her husband.”
But Abimelech had not touched her. He said, “Lord, will you destroy a nation that is unaware and righteous?
Was it not he who told me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself told me, ‘He is my brother.’ I did this with a pure heart and innocent hands.”
God said to him in the dream, “I too knew that you did this with a pure heart, and I restrained you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not return her, know that you will die, you and everyone who belongs to you.”
Abimelech got up early in the morning, called all his servants, and told them all these things. All the men were very afraid of the Lord.

Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? Have we sinned against you, that you have brought a great sin upon me and my kingdom? You have done something to me that no one should do.”
Abimelech said to Abraham, “What were you thinking when you did this?”
Abraham said, “For I thought, ‘Perhaps there is no reverence for God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’
Besides, she really is my sister, on my father’s side but not on my mother’s side, and she became my wife.
When God brought me out of my father’s house, I said to her, ‘This is the kindness you are to show me: wherever we go, say about me, “He is my brother.”’”
Abimelech took five hundred silver staters, sheep, cattle, male slaves, and female slaves and gave them to Abraham. He also returned Sarah his wife.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “Look, the land is before you. Settle in whatever part of the land pleases you.”
He said to Sarah, “Look, I have given your brother five hundred silver staters. These will honor you before everyone who is with you. And tell the truth at all times.”
Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his slaves, and they gave birth.
For God had completely closed every womb in Abimelech’s household because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
The Lord visited Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised.
Sarah became pregnant and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time, just as the Lord had told him.
Abraham named his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore him, Isaac.
Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day, just as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Sarah said, “God has given me laughter, for whoever hears will rejoice with me.”
She said, “Who would have said that Sarah would nurse a child for Abraham? Yet I have given birth to a son in my old age.”
The little child grew, and she weaned him. Abraham held a great feast on the day his son Isaac was weaned.
Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing with Isaac her son.
She said to Abraham, “Drive out this slave woman and her son, for this slave woman’s son must not share the inheritance with my son Isaac.”
This matter was very distressing to Abraham because of his son.
God said to Abraham, “Do not let this matter distress you because of the boy [?]”

Abraham got up early in the morning, took some bread and a waterskin, and gave them to Hagar. She put them on her shoulders. He also gave her the boy and sent her away. She left and wandered in the wilderness near the Well of the Oath.
When the water in the waterskin ran out, she threw the boy under a tree.
She went and sat opposite him at a distance, about a bowshot away, for she said, “I will not watch my son die.” She sat opposite him, and the boy cried out and wept.

God heard the boy’s voice from the place where he was. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the boy’s voice from the place where he is.”

Abraham got up early in the morning and saddled his donkey. He took two slaves with him, along with Isaac his son. He split the wood for the burnt offering, got up, and went to the place God had told him about.

Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac. He took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them walked together.
Isaac said to his father, “Here are the fire, the wood, and the knife. Where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”
Abraham said to him, “God will provide himself with a sheep for the burnt offering, my son,” as the two of them walked together.
They came to the place, and Abraham built an altar to the Lord. He placed the wood on it, bound Isaac his son, and placed him on the altar on top of the wood.
Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slaughter Isaac his son.
But the angel of the Lord called to him from heaven, saying, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Do not lay your hand on the boy or harm him, for I know that you love me and fear God, and you have not spared your beloved son for my sake.”
He looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns under a tree called Sabek. Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of Isaac his son.
Abraham named that place “The Lord Has Seen,” so that people say today, “The Lord appeared on the mountain.”
The angel called to Abraham a second time from heaven, saying:
“I have sworn an oath by myself, says the Lord, because you have done this and have not spared your son, your beloved, for my sake.

Now, therefore, I will surely bless you and make you increase greatly. I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand beside the sea. I will make your descendants inherit the cities of their enemies.

Abraham returned to his servants. They got up and went together to the Well of the Oath, and Abraham settled at the Well of the Oath.
